plan.contextChunk: This figure presents the mass spectrum of chloroethane as a bar-line plot on a pale beige field. The vertical axis reads "Relative abundance (%)" and runs from 0 to 100 with labeled ticks every 20 units; the horizontal axis, labeled "m/z" and followed by a magenta arrow pointing right, spans 10 to 70 with tick marks every 5 units. Inline text near the top center identifies the sample as "CH3CH2Cl" with "MW = 64.5". Each ion is drawn as a thin vertical line whose height encodes its abundance. The densest group sits between about 25 and 30, where three tall lines rise to just above 90 percent and to roughly 85 and 75 percent, with shorter lines beside them and a small cluster near 35 to 37. A medium line near 49 reaches about 25 percent, with a shorter one near 51. At the far right a line at 64 climbs to the full 100 percent and carries the label "M (64)", while a line at 66 reaching about 30 percent is labeled "M + 2"; several short lines fall between 62 and 65. Setting those two labeled lines side by side lets the reader take their height ratio directly, roughly three to one — the signature of an element present as two isotopes in that natural abundance.

interactionPlan.concept: In a mass spectrum, each vertical line's position gives an ion's mass-to-charge ratio and its height gives that ion's relative abundance; for chloroethane the M and M+2 lines at m/z 64 and 66 appear in a ~3:1 ratio, the fingerprint of chlorine's two natural isotopes.
elements: Pale beige plot field with thin black frame
Vertical axis labeled 'Relative abundance (%)' from 0 to 100, labeled ticks every 20
Horizontal axis labeled 'm/z' with a magenta right-pointing arrow after the label, spanning 10 to 70 with ticks every 5
Thin black vertical stick lines representing ions (no bar width, hairline sticks)
Fragment cluster near m/z 25-30: tall lines at ~27 (75%), ~28 (91%), ~29 (85%), shorter lines at ~26 (28%), ~25 (6%), and a very short line near 30-31
Small cluster of short lines near m/z 35-37 (chlorine-containing fragments, ~4-5%)
Medium line at m/z 49 (~25%) with a shorter companion at m/z 51 (~8%) — the CH2Cl+ / isotope pair
Short lines near m/z 47-48 (~3-5%)
Base peak line at m/z 64 reaching 100%, labeled 'M (64)' in italic serif at top right
Line at m/z 66 reaching ~30%, labeled 'M + 2' in italic serif
Several short lines between m/z 62 and 65 (~4-7%) and a tiny line near 67
Inline sample annotation near top center: 'CH3CH2Cl' with subscripts, and 'MW = 64.5' beneath it
Optional bracket/callout connecting the m/z 64 and 66 lines with a '3 : 1' ratio label
Readout tooltip showing m/z and relative abundance for a selected stick

interactions.teaches: Horizontal position of a stick is the ion's mass (m/z) and its height is how frequently that ion forms, so a spectrum is a list of ion masses ranked by abundance.

Selecting the M or M+2 line pairs them, brackets them, and displays their height ratio (~3:1), revealing that the doubled molecular-ion peak comes from 35Cl and 37Cl, not from two different molecules.

interactions.label: Fragment assignments
interactions.teaches: Each major stick corresponds to a specific fragment ion (C2H5+ at 29, CHCl+/CH2Cl+ at 49/51, M at 64), so fragmentation patterns can be read back as pieces of the molecule.

demo_steps.title: Read the axes
demo_steps.narration: Every ion appears as a hairline stick: its position on the m/z axis is its mass, its height is relative abundance scaled so the tallest peak is 100%. Hover any stick to read both numbers at once.

demo_steps.title: The fragment region
demo_steps.narration: Between m/z 25 and 30 the ethyl fragments dominate, and a medium pair sits at 49 and 51. Turning on assignments names the ions responsible for each cluster.

demo_steps.title: The molecular ion and its partner
demo_steps.narration: Click the tall line at m/z 64 (M) to bracket it with the line at m/z 66 (M+2). Their heights stand in a roughly 3:1 ratio — exactly the natural 35Cl : 37Cl abundance — which is why MW is quoted as 64.5 while the spectrum shows a 64 peak.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: A molecular ion that comes in a pair two mass units apart with a 3:1 height ratio is chlorine announcing itself: the spectrum measures individual isotopic molecules, while the periodic-table mass of 64.5 is only their weighted average.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Single panel on a pale beige-to-white vertical gradient with a thin black border. y-axis 'Relative abundance (%)' 0-100, ticks every 20; x-axis 'm/z' 10-70, ticks every 5, with a short magenta arrow drawn to the right of the 'm/z' label. Draw ions as hairline black vertical sticks rising from the baseline, not wide bars. Visual rhythm: a dense tall cluster at 25-30 (peaks ~91, ~85, ~75, plus ~28 and ~6 percent neighbors), a low cluster near 35-37, a medium line at 49 (~25%) with a small partner at 51 (~8%), a few short lines 62-65, a full-height line at 64 labeled 'M (64)' and a ~30% line at 66 labeled 'M + 2', both labels italic serif at the upper and mid right. Centered sample caption 'CH3CH2Cl' (proper subscripts) above 'MW = 64.5'. On click, recolor the 64 and 66 sticks in a saturated accent (magenta) while dimming all others to light gray, and draw a bracket above them carrying '100 : 30 ≈ 3 : 1 (35Cl : 37Cl)'. On hover, dim neighbors and show a small tooltip with 'm/z = N, abundance = X%'.

authoredContext:
The fact that some elements have two common isotopes gives their mass spectra a distinctive appearance. Chlorine, for example, exists as two isotopes, 35Cl and 37Cl, in roughly a 3: 1 ratio. In a sample of chloroethane, three out of four molecules contain a 35Cl atom and one out of four has a 37Cl atom. In the mass spectrum of chloroethane (the figure we see the molecular ion (M) at m/z = 64 for ions that contain a 35Cl and another peak at m/z = 66, called the M + 2 peak, for ions containing a 37Cl. The ratio of the relative abundance of M: M + 2 is about 3: 1, a reflection of the isotopic abundances of chlorine.

Mass spectrum of chloroethane.

The mass spectrum of chloroethane with two peaks at m / z 64 and 66, labeled M and M + 2, on a 3 to 1 height ratio.

In the case of bromine, the isotopic distribution is 50.7% 79Br and 49.3% 81Br. In the mass spectrum of 1-bromohexane (the figure) the molecular ion appears at m/z = 164 for 79Br-containing ions and the M + 2 peak is at m/z = 166 for 81Br-containing ions. The ions at m/z = 135 and 137 are informative as well. The two nearly equally large peaks tell us that the ions at those m/z values still contain the bromine atom. The peak at m/z = 85, on the other hand, does not contain bromine because there is not a large peak at m/z = 87.

discrepancies: All axis tick labels are missing in the rendered figure: the x-axis numbers 10,15,…,70 and the y-axis numbers 0,20,…,100 present in the source do not appear — the plugin's beforeDatasetsDraw fills the whole canvas white, painting over the scale layers (which Chart.js v4 draws at z≤0, i.e. before datasets).
The y-axis title 'Relative abundance (%)' from the source is configured but also erased by the same white fill, so the figure has no vertical axis label at all.
Tick marks and the L-shaped axis borders are likewise wiped out; only the plugin-drawn rectangular frame remains, so the plot reads as a bare box rather than the source's ticked axes.

Because the y-axis label/tick gutter is blanked, the plot area is shifted and the 'CH₃CH₂Cl / MW = 64.5' caption sits noticeably left of centre compared with the source, where it is centred over the 35–50 region.

Minor: the source shows a cluster of very small peaks around m/z 30–31 and 47–48 with slightly different relative heights; generated values are plausible but not identical (extra 38, 61, 65, 67 sticks not clearly present in the source).
evaluation.notes: Stick-spectrum geometry, peak pattern, gradient background and the M/M+2 pedagogy are all faithful and the step player plus assignment toggle are genuinely useful, but the background-fill plugin erases every axis tick label, tick mark and the 'Relative abundance (%)' title, leaving an unlabelled box that no longer works as a drop-in replacement for the source.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction design are sound (concept_accuracy 5); the sole failure is an implementation bug where the background-fill plugin draws over the axis layers, erasing ticks and titles — a concrete code-level fix.

discrepancies: Aspect ratio/composition: the source plot is portrait (tall, narrow), while the generated chart is wide and vertically compressed, so the 25–30 fragment cluster and the 64/66 pair sit closer together horizontally than in the original.
Stick weight: source peaks are true hairlines (<1 px); generated bars are ~2–3 px wide with slightly softer edges, giving the cluster at m/z 26–29 a blockier look.
Caption block 'CH₃CH₂Cl / MW = 64.5' is placed a bit left and with wider line spacing than the source, and sits lower relative to the 91% peak top.
Y-axis extends to 110 (extra headroom above 100) whereas the source frame tops out just above 100, so the M (64) peak does not reach as near the frame top as in the original.
Added elements not in the source: fragment-assignment leader lines/callouts and the pink 100:30 isotope bracket (both gated behind toggles/steps, default off, so only a mild addition).
evaluation.notes: A close, well-composed reproduction of the chloroethane mass spectrum with correct peak positions/intensities, the beige gradient field, italic M (64) / M + 2 labels and the magenta m/z arrow, backed by genuinely useful interactions (3-step player, assignment toggle, M/M+2 highlight, hover readout); weaknesses are the wider aspect ratio, slightly thick sticks, extra y headroom, and caption placement drift.
action_items: Reduce barThickness to ~1–1.5 px (or draw 1 px lines) and set the y-axis max to ~105 so the base peak nearly touches the frame as in the source.
Constrain the plot frame to a taller, more portrait aspect (or increase container height) so the horizontal peak spacing matches the original spectrum.
Tighten the two caption lines (CH₃CH₂Cl / MW = 64.5) to the source's spacing and recenter them around m/z ≈ 40 at y ≈ 85/79.
When the pair is highlighted, check that the repositioned 'M (64)' label at y=95 does not collide with the isotope bracket or the m/z 64 stick.

feedback.rationale: Concept and interaction structure are sound; remaining issues are concrete rendering details (bar thickness, axis max, aspect ratio, caption placement) that belong to the generator.

discrepancies: The 'M (64)' label is pinned to the top-right corner of the frame (right-aligned to the plot edge) rather than sitting directly above the m/z 64 stick as in the source; similarly 'M + 2' hugs the right border instead of sitting just right of the m/z 66 stick, giving both labels a slightly crowded, edge-clipped feel.
The y-axis title 'Relative abundance (%)' and the tick labels are rendered noticeably smaller/lighter than in the source, where the axis label is a prominent element of the composition.

Small extra sticks are present around m/z 30–31, 38, 47, 61 and 65 that are hard to see or absent in the source; conversely the source's tiny peak at ~m/z 50 region is approximated differently — negligible but a slight fabrication of low-abundance detail.

The default state adds no non-source chrome, but step 3 introduces a magenta isotope bracket and '100 : 30 ≈ 3 : 1' annotation plus recoloured M/M+2 labels that do not exist in the source (acceptable as an interactive overlay, but it changes the palette from the all-black sticks).
evaluation.notes: A highly faithful reproduction of the chloroethane mass spectrum — correct hairline sticks, axis ranges/ticks, beige gradient field, caption and m/z arrow — backed by genuinely useful interactions (step player, assignment callouts, M/M+2 highlight, hover readout); only minor label-placement and label-size issues keep it from perfect.

feedback.rationale: No failure modes or action items remain and all core dimensions score 5 with only negligible label-placement nitpicks, so the figure is good enough to stop iterating.

discrepancies: The 'M (64)' label is pinned to the top-right corner of the frame (right-aligned to the plot edge) rather than sitting directly above the m/z 64 stick as in the source; similarly 'M + 2' hugs the right border instead of sitting just right of the m/z 66 stick, giving both labels a slightly crowded, edge-clipped feel.
The y-axis title 'Relative abundance (%)' and the tick labels are rendered noticeably smaller/lighter than in the source, where the axis label is a prominent element of the composition.

Small extra sticks are present around m/z 30–31, 38, 47, 61 and 65 that are hard to see or absent in the source; conversely the source's tiny peak at ~m/z 50 region is approximated differently — negligible but a slight fabrication of low-abundance detail.

The default state adds no non-source chrome, but step 3 introduces a magenta isotope bracket and '100 : 30 ≈ 3 : 1' annotation plus recoloured M/M+2 labels that do not exist in the source (acceptable as an interactive overlay, but it changes the palette from the all-black sticks).
